findings.reason: without an ordering relationship or an exclusion line a coordinator can dispatch §50 first, which makes §39's 47,000 measure unreachable and sends its worker past the named family hunting for tokens to move.
findings.text: §39's Why asserts "a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline §50 writes `reckon/roadmap.py` next, so the split leaves it room", yet §39 declares no gate or dependency on §50 and, unlike §36's "Do not build it while read-deadline §38 is in flight", states no concurrent-build exclusion; §50 is `implementable` and names `reckon/roadmap.py` among its write paths, so §50 landing first both collides in the file and grows the module, and §39's done-when ("`reckon/roadmap.py` measures at most 47,000 estimated tokens") then measures a head the split can no longer reach

findings.reason: the plan's own mechanism is "imports `reckon.roadmap` inside the functions that need it, at call time", which covers every such name however many there are, so an exhaustive list changes the prose and not the work.
findings.text: the Deliverable states the reverse dependency as a definite list ("`resolve_graph_target` calls back into code that stays: `build_roadmap`, `_plan_decision_sections`, `unsettled_decisions`, `closure_blockers`, `_whole_plan_dependency` and `_judgment_member`"), but the moved region also calls `_status` (`reckon/roadmap.py:618`, at :2574, :2596, :2655, :2818), `_progress` (`:132`, at :2656, :2819) and `_decision_rows` (`:1014`, at :2822), and raises `GraphTargetError` (`:124`), all of which stay
